Bring a question or a piece of work into a conversation. A small reproduction,
an honest failure or a useful explanation gives someone else something to engage with.

## Choose how to participate

```{=html}
<div class="participation-grid"><article><h3>Ask and help</h3><p>A precise question, a reproduction or an explanation.</p><small>Forums, Discord, Slack and office hours.</small></article><article><h3>Reproduce and compare</h3><p>A small test of a paper, demo or technical claim.</p><small>Paper clubs, GitHub discussions and research groups.</small></article><article><h3>Contribute</h3><p>A test, documentation fix, example or bounded code change.</p><small>Open-source projects and their contribution channels.</small></article><article><h3>Build together</h3><p>A specific part of a shared problem.</p><small>Project groups, hackathons, research jams and meetups.</small></article><article><h3>Explain and demonstrate</h3><p>A useful account of something you actually tried.</p><small>A repo, Substack, LinkedIn, YouTube or a live demo.</small></article><article><h3>Maintain and convene</h3><p>Continued care for a useful tool or exchange.</p><small>A repository, study group or recurring community session.</small></article></div>
```

## Find a useful first contribution

Start with a problem you can reproduce. These are project entry points, rather than a list of issues claimed to be open.

```{=html}
<div class="project-routes"><article><div><h3><a href="https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/inspector" class="" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">MCP Inspector</a></h3><p>Makes protocol and server behavior easier to inspect and test.</p></div><div><p>Improve a reproducible validation error or add a targeted regression test for a server-response edge case.</p><a href="https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/inspector/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md" class="" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Read the contribution guide</a></div></article><article><div><h3><a href="https://github.com/huggingface/datasets" class="" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Hugging Face Datasets</a></h3><p>Data preparation and dataset behavior are central AI engineering skills beyond model APIs.</p></div><div><p>Create a tiny fixture reproducing a real schema, streaming, or serialization bug, then offer a bounded test/fix.</p><a href="https://github.com/huggingface/datasets/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md" class="" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Read the contribution guide</a></div></article><article><div><h3><a href="https://github.com/promptfoo/promptfoo" class="" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">promptfoo</a></h3><p>A practical way to turn AI behavior into repeatable test cases and compare configurations.</p></div><div><p>Fix a genuinely broken example or add a small assertion/provider regression case backed by a local reproduction.</p><a href="https://www.promptfoo.dev/docs/contributing/" class="" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Read the contribution guide</a></div></article><article><div><h3><a href="https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack" class="" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Haystack</a></h3><p>Explicit components and pipelines make retrieval and generation behavior easier to reason about.</p></div><div><p>Add a tiny fixture and regression test for an observed document-filter or pipeline-component bug.</p><a href="https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md" class="" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Read the contribution guide</a></div></article><article><div><h3><a href="https://github.com/Arize-ai/phoenix" class="" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Arize Phoenix</a></h3><p>A concrete way to learn what an AI application does through traces and evaluation records.</p></div><div><p>Reproduce an import or trace-display issue using a tiny sanitized trace fixture and propose a targeted test/fix.</p><a href="https://github.com/Arize-ai/phoenix/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md" class="" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Read the contribution guide</a></div></article></div>
```

## Let the work lead to the conversation

**Question → small experiment → inspectable artifact → useful exchange → a better question.**

A short demonstration can show what you expected, what happened and what you are still trying to understand.
Teaching from that evidence is one way to develop a public voice. It does not require a large audience.

An involvement scout can eventually connect current questions and experiments to specific projects,
discussions or collaboration calls. A useful recommendation should explain the fit, what you could bring,
the smallest first action and whether the opportunity is currently open. That scouting process has not been automated here.
